header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (Redwood Product), Priya Singh (Aurora Head of Partnerships), Diego Ramirez (Aurora Cloud Architect), Anika Bose (Aurora Security), Marcus Yu (Aurora Marketplace PM)
summary: Partner technical sync to align on Redwood marketplace listing and joint reference architecture. Discussed listing requirements, packaging (images, BOM, support information), reference architecture options for marketplace deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private), network/connectivity patterns, credential flow and KMS integration, and a quick plan for a smoke benchmark. Agreed on next steps: Redwood to share checklist and run a benchmark; Aurora to share network diagrams and compliance requirements. Security deep dive to be scheduled.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we should be able to stick to 45 minutes, couple of folks from Aurora, hi!
[00:05] Priya Singh: Hi Maya, thanks for setting this up. we wanted to make sure the marketplace listing is smooth and then talk about a reference arch for our customers.
[00:12] Liam Chen: Great, quick intros — I'm Liam, Redwood SE, I’ll be driving the technical bits and the smoke bench.
[00:18] Diego Ramirez: Diego here, cloud architect. we run multiple regions, prefer to understand network reqs and any IP whitelisting.
[00:24] Sofia Patel: Sofia, product — I'll help with the listing metadata and screenshots guidance.
[00:28] Anika Bose: Anika from security — I'll surface SOC2 and key management questions.
[00:32] Marcus Yu: Marcus, marketplace PM at Aurora, I'll own the listing flow on our side.
[00:36] Maya Thompson: Cool, agenda: marketplace checklist, reference arch options, network and security, benchmarks, and next steps. sound good?
[00:42] Priya Singh: Yep.
[00:45] Maya: Ok starting with marketplace listing. Sofia, do you want to walk through what we typically require?
[00:50] Sofia: Sure. For Aurora we'll need a short blurb, long description, 2-3 screenshots or architecture diagrams, a one-line tagline, pricing model (we support both metered and subscription), support contact and SLAs, logos, and a BOM — like which Redwood product offering: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private. We also ask for a reference architecture diagram for the listing page that maps to Aurora deployment types.
[01:12] Marcus: On the screenshots, is it ok to include console screenshots? we tend to blur customer data.
[01:16] Sofia: Yes console screenshots are fine, just redact PII. we can also provide a mock console template if helpful.
[01:21] Priya: What about the product SKU or package naming? we need guidance so it appears correctly in the marketplace catalog.
[01:26] Maya: We'll provide recommended SKU mapping — e.g., redwood-hosted-standard, redwood-dedicated-1gpu, redwood-private-onprem. we'll include examples in the checklist.
[01:34] Diego: For dedicated and private, we need to see the reference arch, especially around network egress and peering. do you have standard diagrams?
[01:42] Liam: Yes. we have reference architectures for three modes: hosted (SaaS), dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool in our infra), and private (VPC or on-prem bundle). Each map shows control plane flow, data plane routing, KMS calls, and audit log flow. I'll attach those.
[01:56] Diego: Quick question — in dedicated mode, is traffic backhauled through Redwood control plane or does it stay in-region?
[02:03] Liam: Good question. Dedicated keeps inference in the customer-dedicated pool in the region; control plane signals (model updates, metrics) may talk to our control plane over the management endpoint, but inference traffic does not need to egress to Redwood hosted endpoints if configured for private networking. for Marketplace listing we should call out options and recommended topology.
[02:23] Anika: From security, need details on encryption at rest, KMS integration, and whether logs contain PII. also SSO/SAML for admin console.
[02:31] Maya: Absolutely. Redwood supports KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, external HSMs for private), and audit logs can be routed to syslog/S3/Splunk — we'll document retention.
[02:41] Anika: Great, do you have SOC2 cert? Aurora will require evidence for the listing.
[02:45] Sofia: We have SOC2 Type II — I can attach certification and our security pack.
[02:50] Priya: on billing — how do usage and metering show up in Aurora's billing? do you support marketplace billing connectors?
[02:57] Maya: We support both direct billing and marketplace metering integrations. For Aurora marketplace we can do metered usage feed; Marcus, can you share the technical spec for your metering API?
[03:06] Marcus: yes i'll send the spec after the call. typically we accept hourly or token-based usage reports.
[03:11] Diego: Network again — any static IP ranges to allow for management traffic? we run strict firewalls.
[03:16] Liam: We publish a CIDR set for management endpoints; for private/dedicated customers we can set up VPC peering or private links. i'll include the CIDR list and note ephemeral ranges for some services.
[03:26] Marcus: timeline — what's a typical time to get a listing live?
[03:29] Sofia: If all assets and security docs are provided, 2 weeks to review and publish, sometimes quicker.
[03:34] Priya: good. ok moving to reference architecture — Diego, do you have constraints or a preferred topology?
[03:40] Diego: We generally prefer not to route inference through third-party public endpoints. for regulated customers, they want data residency and no egress. private deployment is interesting but we need packaging that is easy to deploy in Aurora regions.
[03:52] Liam: For that we recommend Redwood Private: control plane can be customers-managed, or we can deploy a private control plane in Aurora VPC. for easier onboarding we also offer an appliance-like on-prem install. The RA (reference architecture) will show either VPC peering with private endpoints or an air-gapped on-prem path.
[04:10] Anika: For KMS, crucial that keys never leave customer KMS. do you support customer-managed keys for model weights and logs?
[04:18] Liam: Keys for customer data are customer-managed. for model weights in hosted public catalog, weights are in Redwood storage; for private/dedicated we can enable BYOK (bring your own key) and encrypt at rest with customer KMS. we'll put that in the security doc.
[04:31] Diego: On performance: we want to run a smoke benchmark with our dev region to measure cold-start and p95 latency for our common request size. can Redwood run a short benchmark?
[04:40] Liam: Yes, we can. We'll need an API key or temporary dev creds and a test dataset. It'll be a smoke run — not exhaustive but will surface major issues. estimate about 2-3 hours to run then share logs.
[04:53] Priya: do you need access to our VPC or just to a public endpoint?
[04:57] Liam: For hosted it's public endpoint; for private/dedicated we'd prefer a peered environment. for the smoke bench we can start with hosted in your dev region, then iterate.
[05:05] Maya: Action item — Liam will run the benchmark; Diego will provide dev region endpoint details.
[05:10] Marcus: On support SLAs for marketplace customers, what are typical tiers?
[05:14] Sofia: We offer Standard (business hours), Priority (24x7 incident response) and Enterprise (designated TAM + SLA). We'll include the support matrix.
[05:22] Anika: Can you confirm audit log retention windows and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM?
[05:26] Liam: Yes logs can be exported; retention configurable — default 90 days, longer with add-on. We can forward events to Splunk, Datadog, S3.
[05:33] Diego: Regarding deployment automation, do you publish terraform modules or helm charts for private deployments?
[05:38] Sofia: We have terraform module examples and helm charts for on-prem/k8s installs. we'll link to our github repo in the checklist.
[05:46] Priya: Great. Marcus, on the marketplace side, any additional requirements we should be aware of?
[05:50] Marcus: Our listing requires a support email, legal contact, POC, and a trial period setup if you want a "Try it" button. trials need to be time-limited and instrumented for usage.
[05:58] Maya: Redwood can enable trial credits for marketplace signups; we'll template the trial workflow.
[06:03] Anika: One more security note — do you have a hardened image for Dedicated/Private with minimal outbound services?
[06:09] Liam: We do; hardened images are used for private installs, and we can lock down outbound egress to only KMS endpoints and local telemetry sinks — we'll document the ports and endpoints.
[06:20] Priya: Ok let's talk visuals for the listing — can you provide a reference architecture svg and a 2-slide mgmt console screenshot?
[06:26] Sofia: Yes. I'll attach an SVG RA and a mock console PNG.
[06:30] Diego: On latency expectations for 8k token contexts — what are your p95 numbers on A100-like hardware?
[06:36] Liam: For well-optimized models we typically see p95 sub-200ms for single-turn 512-token requests on our dedicated GPU pool; longer contexts scale linearly — we'll include model profilers in the benchmark deliverable. caveat: depends on quantization and batch settings.
[06:52] Priya: Sounds good. anything on observability? we want per-route latency and cost breakdowns surfaced in our billing portal.
[06:58] Sofia: Redwood Console exposes per-route token-level cost and latency, and can push usage metrics to your billing system via webhook or metering feed. we'll include sample payloads.
[07:08] Maya: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: Maya/Sofia to share listing checklist, Liam to run smoke benchmark, Diego to share network/dev details, Anika to send compliance list, Marcus to share marketplace metering API. We'll schedule a security deep dive next week.
[07:23] Priya: Thanks all, this was helpful.
[07:25] Maya: Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite.
[07:30] [End of recording]
